annotatedSteps.description: Expressing speed and times taken in terms of x
annotatedSteps.studentWork: Let the speed of the train be x km/h. Reduced speed = (x − 8) km/h. Time at usual speed = 480/x, time at reduced speed = 480/(x − 8).
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Correct representation of speed and times in terms of x.

annotatedSteps.description: Formulating the equation relating the two times
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: × Incorrect equation order: reduced speed takes more time, so 480/(x − 8) > 480/x.

annotatedSteps.description: Simplifying the equation to standard quadratic form (ECF)
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Simplification carried out correctly from the student's formed equation (ECF).
× Incorrect factorisation: (x − 40)(x + 32) expands to x² − 8x − 1280, not x² − 8x + 1280.

annotatedSteps.description: Finding roots, rejecting negative value and stating final speed with unit
annotatedSteps.studentWork: ⇒ x = 40 or x = −32. Speed cannot be negative. ∴ Speed of the train = 40 km/h.
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Correct roots from factors, negative root correctly rejected, and unit included.

teacherNote: Remember that lower speed means greater time, so you must subtract the smaller time from the larger time: 480/(x − 8) − 480/x = 3. Because of the initial order reversal, your equation had +1280, which does not factor into (x − 40)(x + 32). Be careful with signs when setting up rate-time problems.

rubric.point: Assuming speed as x km/h and expressing times in terms of x
Simplifying the equation to standard quadratic form
Solving the quadratic equation by factorisation or quadratic formula
Rejecting the negative root with reason and stating final speed with units
